name: input-otp
behavior: Native text-input semantics on a single visually segmented field. ONE control owns the value, the focus and the tab stop (inputMode=numeric, autoComplete=one-time-code, maxLength=length); the cells are presentational (aria-hidden) and mirror the control's characters, with the caret drawn on the active cell. ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End/Backspace therefore behave natively, paste fills every cell at once, and screen readers announce one field — never N fields. Labelling and error wiring come from the field composition.

parts.note: the wrapper; hosts the single control and the cell rows
the one real input — visually hidden over the cells, carrying the whole value
a run of adjacent cells; multiple groups exist only when a separator splits the code

parts.statesNote: the cell under the caret takes field-border-active plus the focus ring; invalid swaps field-border for status-critical per states.md

the dash between cell groups; aria-hidden

anatomyNotes: shadcn InputOTP (input-otp library) is the only source with this component; Salt has no equivalent, so the intersection is taken against Salt Input for the cell chrome — a cell is a one-character input face and reuses field-border/field-surface/radius-control exactly, which is why Salt can theme it without new slots. shadcn draws cells as a segmented strip with only the outer corners rounded; that is a RECIPE on the group, not anatomy — themes that round every cell (Salt's per-field chrome) render the same parts.
